commit.message:
feat(sim): judge fixture collisions against the fixture's real mesh

The world-AABB fixture laws (c2)/(d2) stay the broad phase; a tagged
model's closed world mesh now gets the last word on every upright move
its box flagged, and may only acquit. A path down a vise's gap - inside
its one box, nowhere near its steel - posts and generates clean, while
a jaw-corner clip, a rapid into a jaw top, a holder over a jaw and a
tool buried in steel still block the post.

Narrow phase (camcraft_sim::fixture_mesh): each band of the stack is an
upright cylinder swept along the tip's chord - a convex Minkowski sum -
tested against facets by GJK, "clear" only on a proven support-plane gap
over FIXTURE_HIT_TOL (+ the arc chord's deviation); a band clear of
every facet is decided wholly inside/outside by ray-crossing winding +
parity with ambiguity rejection. Object-median AABB BVH, pruned by the
same proof. Open, non-finite, collapsed or oversized meshes refuse by
name (MeshError) and keep the box verdict; posed, C-turned, XZ/YZ-arc
moves and lathe tools keep the box verdict. Where nothing is acquitted
the report is the box laws' own, byte for byte.

Refs #339

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge remote-tracking branch 'upstream/main' (#381 HolderStack) into issue/339-fixture-mesh

#381 landed: the fixture laws read a HolderStack. The mesh law follows:
steel_stack takes the same HolderStack (shank, the holder's own bands,
the housing on holder.top), and mesh_refined wraps the *_held laws in
posting::fixture_problems and generate::workholding_warnings - so a
modelled holder body is judged against the fixture mesh band by band.

feat(ui): fixture UX - mark/import from the browser, mesh state, struck tint

#339 slice 4. A model row's context menu offers "Use as fixture" (bound
to the active setup) / "Stop using as fixture" through the existing
TagFixture / UntagFixture commands; a setup's Fixtures node offers
"Import fixture…", which now lands mesh and marker as one undo unit
(new ImportFixture command; it was two).

Each Fixtures row shows how the gate judges the steel: "mesh" or
"box only: <reason>" from #476's MeshError (open mesh, non-finite,
collapsed, over the facet cap, no facets) or a shared box. The Fixtures
page prints the full sentence. app::fixture_view computes it, cached
per document version.

When the selected op has FixtureHit warnings, app::fixture_struck
judges each fixture on its own with the post gate's per-op law
(op_hits, which posting::fixture_problems now shares). The fixtures
that reproduce a warned move are tinted in the viewport (vertex class
STRUCK_CLASS -> gouge colour) and named in the op banner. A warned move
that no fixture reproduces is reported as unresolved and nothing is
tinted for it. This is display only.

Refs #339

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge upstream/main (70c261ba) into issue/339-fixture-mesh-v2

Brings in #464 (fixture-law gaps: stack_span upright rapids + ramps),
#462 (carry-machine check) and #470 (MCP setup/machine/fixture tools).

Conflict resolutions:
- crates/app/src/posting.rs fixture_findings: main (#181/#470) made the
  walk return Result<FixtureFindings, String> with (name, hit) pairs and
  an unjudged list; #476 wraps both *_held laws in mesh_refined with
  steel_stack(geom, holder, spindle) and a per-setup mesh cache. Kept
  both: the mesh-refined bands and rapids hits feed out.hits, the mesh
  refusals are still logged once per setup, and the walk returns
  Ok(out). fixture_problems is main's (strings from the findings), so
  the gate and the MCP get_fixture_findings tool both see the
  mesh-refined verdict.
- Sim side (no textual conflict): #464 rewrote laws (c2)/(d2) through
  stack_span. mesh_refined calls the laws through its closure, so it
  wraps the new laws unchanged; steel_stack is the same band list as
  stack_span::upper_bands plus the flute. One semantic fix: judge_move
  labelled every rapid hit FixturePart::Rapid, but (d2) now names a
  band above the flute by its part - the mesh now does the same (only
  the flute reads as Rapid). Pinned by sim fixture_mesh
  a_rapid_kept_by_the_mesh_names_its_band_like_law_d2 (fails on the
  old label). Recorded in docs/decisions/339-fixture-mesh.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge issue/339-fixture-mesh-v2 (with upstream/main 70c261ba) into issue/339-fixture-ux

Takes the parent PR #476 after its merge of upstream/main (#464
stack_span, #462 carry-machine check, #470 MCP setup/machine/fixture
tools), so this branch is current with main too.

Conflict resolution:
- crates/app/src/posting.rs: #470 split the gate walk into
  fixture_problems (strings) over fixture_findings ->
  Result<FixtureFindings, String> (hits as (op, warning) pairs plus an
  unjudged list), which #476 carried with the mesh_refined *_held laws
  inline. This branch had moved that per-op law into
  fixture_struck::op_hits so the viewport tint and the gate share it.
  Kept the refactor: fixture_findings calls op_hits once per op (which
  holds #476's mesh_refined bands/rapids with steel_stack and #368's
  tool_body::judged), Ok hits go to out.hits, Err (a body that no
  longer fits its tool) goes to out.unjudged as "{op}: tool T: why" -
  the exact string main produced. fixture_problems stays main's, so
  the gate, the MCP get_fixture_findings tool and the struck-fixture
  tint all read one law.

feat(app): fixture library - save, insert and delete user fixtures

A user fixture library (#339 slice 6): one `fixtures.camfixtures` file
in the user fixtures folder (CAMCRAFT_FIXTURES, else
<data dir>/camcraft/fixtures, beside #383's machines folder), in a
versioned `camcraft-fixtures/1` JSON envelope shaped like the tool
library's. Each entry is a name, an optional note, the mesh in the
fixture's own model frame, and the placement datum inside that frame.

- app::fixture_library: a strict reader that refuses the whole file by
  entry name, and a byte-stable writer. The store resolves the folder,
  writes atomically, asks before replacing a name (Exists), and deletes
  an entry.
- commands::InsertFixture: one undo unit. It adds a model with the
  entry's facets, places it at P ∘ D⁻¹ so the datum lands on the pick,
  and tags it to the setup. A name already in the document takes
  "(2)". The result is an ordinary tagged model, with no new project
  key.
- ui: the Fixtures node menu gains "Save fixture to library…" and
  "Insert from library…". Both open modal dialogs: checked fixtures,
  datum and note for a save; the entry list, datum origin and rotation,
  Insert, and Delete with a confirmation for an insert.

Pinned by app fixture_library (6) and ui fixture_library_tests (4).
The slice-4 menu-label test now lists the two new rows.

Refs #339
